about: The asset-library pages (site/models.ts): one per kind of model, in priority order (a model shows on the first page that chooses it). words/not/types/styles/animated/rigged/license match catalog rows; demand is the threads that show people building with this kind of model in three.js, with views read on 2026-10-28; notes is the page's own text; reject is what the review of the page's thumbnails left out.

categories.title: Free tree 3D models for three.js (GLB, CC BY)

demand.title: Can we create realistic trees with textures in threejs?
Seeking optimization tips: big map with trees and rocks

categories.notes:
Most leafy trees here draw their canopy as flat cards cut out by a leaf texture's alpha channel. Give those materials `alphaTest` and `side: THREE.DoubleSide` and leave `transparent` off: alpha testing writes depth, so the leaves need no sorting and stop flickering as the camera turns. The low-poly ones (860 of the 1,536 that pass) are solid shapes in flat colours and need neither.

For a forest, load one tree and copy each of its meshes into an `InstancedMesh`, one per mesh and material, giving every copy a random turn and a slightly different scale. Hundreds of trees then cost a handful of draw calls. Far from the camera, swap the detailed model for a low-poly stand-in with `THREE.LOD`. Each tree is scaled to its real height (6 m for the median one), which keeps a forest in proportion with a player of human size. Of these, 73 are animated; play their clips through an `AnimationMixer`.

categories.title: Free palm tree 3D models for three.js (GLB, CC BY)
categories.notes:
A palm is a bare trunk under a crown of fronds, and the fronds hold the cost and the trouble. In the textured palms each frond is a card cut out by its texture's alpha: set `alphaTest` on that material and draw both faces with `THREE.DoubleSide`, or the far half of the crown vanishes when seen from below. The low-poly palms (72 of the 144 that pass) use folded strips in flat colour instead.

A row of palms along a road suits an `InstancedMesh` per part. To make the crown sway, patch the material's vertex shader with `onBeforeCompile`, bending each vertex by a sine of time weighted by its world height (apply `modelMatrix` first, since meshopt stores positions quantized to the mesh's bounds): conversion for the web removed each file's node hierarchy and fused fronds drawn with one material into a single mesh, leaving no node per frond to rotate. The median palm stands 8 m tall at real size.

categories.title: Free flower 3D models for three.js (GLB, CC BY)
categories.notes:
Flowers are small: the median one stands 0.5 m high at life size, so frame them for a close, low camera; in a view sized for buildings they shrink to specks. Petals and leaves are thin sheets, often one-sided in the source file; if a petal disappears when seen from behind, set `side: THREE.DoubleSide` on that material. Textured petals with cut-out edges want `alphaTest` as well.

Triangle counts vary widely, with the middle half between 1,670 and 36,700, and a bed of the heavy ones adds up fast. For a flower bed, take a light model, read its meshes (stem, petals and leaves stay apart when they use separate materials) and build one `InstancedMesh` for each, sharing the same instance matrices so the parts stay together; `setColorAt()` then gives every copy its own petal tint from a single material. A bouquet model holds several stems in one mesh, so it makes a centrepiece but scatters poorly. Check a picked file with `model_audit` before planting a hundred.

categories.title: Free plant 3D models for three.js (GLB, CC BY)

demand.title: [Paid][Remote] Looking for Three.js dev to create generative ecosystem of organisms and plants
Plant geometry for large GLTF-based scenes

categories.notes:
Most of these are houseplants and garden plants at real size, many with a pot whose base sits on the origin, so a plant placed at a shelf's top height stands on the shelf. Leaves cut from a texture need `alphaTest` and `THREE.DoubleSide`; broad modelled leaves usually do not.

When a scene holds many plants, reuse instead of reloading. Load each file once and place copies with `gltf.scene.clone()`: a clone shares the original's geometry and materials, so extra copies add draw calls but no memory. Past a few dozen copies, an `InstancedMesh` per mesh brings each mesh down to one draw call. Mixed styles look wrong side by side in one room, and this category spans stylized (452), realistic (266) and low-poly (227), so pick from one. A realistic plant with dense foliage can run past the upper quartile of 25,500 triangles; run `model_audit` on it and keep the light ones where many are seen at once.

categories.title: Free rock 3D models for three.js (GLB, CC BY and CC0)

demand.title: Seeking optimization tips: big map with trees and rocks

categories.notes:
Rocks repeat more than other props, so the work is hiding the repetition. Load several different rocks, then scatter each through an `InstancedMesh` with a random rotation on all three axes and an uneven scale (stretch one axis a little); one rock seen at many angles reads as many rocks. Sink each copy slightly into the ground so no gap shows beneath it: its origin is the bottom of its bounds, so a rock set at ground height merely touches it.

Scanned and realistic rocks carry their look in a normal map and a detailed colour texture. Dense ones go past the 37,000 triangles of the upper quartile here, and `model_audit` shows the count and texture sizes before you place hundreds. For physics, give a rock a sphere, box or convex-hull collider, never the render mesh. On a large map, split the scatter into one `InstancedMesh` per area: three.js culls an instanced mesh as a whole, by the sphere around all its instances, so a single map-wide one is drawn every frame.

categories.title: Free terrain 3D models for three.js (GLB, CC BY)

demand.title: How to make character walk on custom terrain made in Blender?
Dynamic terrain deformation under a polygon / road (GLB terrain ~30k vertices)

categories.notes:
A terrain model here is a sculpted piece: a hill, a mountain, a valley diorama or a floating landscape, mostly low-poly (102 of the 204 that pass). Real sizes vary a great deal, since some authors modelled a whole mountain at full scale; pick with a `height` to get it in your scene's units, and set the camera's `far` plane to cover it.

To walk a character over it, cast a ray straight down from above the character each frame with `THREE.Raycaster` against the terrain mesh and set the character's height from the hit point. A raycast tests every triangle, so for a dense terrain add the `three-mesh-bvh` library and call `computeBoundsTree()` on the geometry, which makes each cast cheap. These pieces are closed sculpted scenery, not heightmaps: to deform the ground under a road or a footprint, build that patch as a `PlaneGeometry` whose vertices you can move, and blend it into the model at its edges.

categories.title: Free floating island 3D models for three.js (GLB, CC BY)
categories.notes:
Islands are whole small scenes in one file: ground, trees, a house, water, sometimes clouds, and 48 of them animated. That suits a portfolio centrepiece or a level's backdrop, less so a repeated prop. Check one with `look` before you light it: many were built to be seen from outside at a three-quarter angle, with no underside, or with a cone of rock beneath a floating base.

Play the animated ones with an `AnimationMixer`: `mixer.clipAction(gltf.animations[0]).play()`, then `mixer.update(delta)` each frame. A floating island with no animation comes alive with a slow bob, a sine of time added to `position.y`, and a slight turn. Water in these files is usually a flat mesh, opaque or slightly transparent; if it flickers against the shore, it sits too close to the ground beneath it, so raise it a little. Parts with a common material were fused when the file was prepared, so a diorama's draw calls follow how many materials it uses, and `perf` reports them.

categories.title: Free crystal 3D models for three.js (GLB, CC BY and CC0)
categories.notes:
A crystal's look is mostly its material, and GLTFLoader gives these files a `MeshStandardMaterial`, which renders a gem as coloured plastic rather than glass. For glass-like gems, replace it with `MeshPhysicalMaterial` and set `transmission`, `ior`, `thickness` and a low `roughness`. Transmission refracts what lies behind the gem and needs surroundings to show, so give the scene an environment: `PMREMGenerator` turns the `RoomEnvironment` addon into `scene.environment` with no image to load. `flatShading: true` keeps facets crisp on the low-poly gems.

For a magical glow, raise `emissive` and `emissiveIntensity` and add `UnrealBloomPass` from the postprocessing addons; bloom picks up whatever passes its threshold, so keep the rest of the scene darker. Transmission costs an extra render of the scene each frame, fine for a few hero gems and too much for a cave lined with them, where emissive crystals without transmission do the job. The median crystal is 0.3 m tall, a hand-held size, so a cluster meant to tower over a player needs a `height` at pick time.

categories.title: Free planet 3D models for three.js (GLB, CC BY and CC0)
categories.notes:
Many planet files record the real diameter as their height, so a picked Earth can arrive thousands of kilometres across: the camera ends up inside it or the far plane cuts it, and the page shows nothing. That is a frequent reason a planet GLB seems not to load. Pick with a `height` (say 2) to get it in scene units, or scale it yourself, and confirm with `look` that it is in view.

Spin a planet about its own axis with `rotation.y += speed * delta`. For a moon, add it to an empty `Object3D` at the planet's centre and turn that pivot, which makes the moon orbit with no trigonometry. A second sphere slightly larger than the planet, with `side: THREE.BackSide`, additive blending and a blue tint, makes a cheap atmosphere rim. No planet here has a 2048 px map, and close up the surface turns soft; keep the camera at a distance or add a normal map. Of these, 11 are animated, mostly turning in place.

categories.title: Free car 3D models for three.js (GLB, CC BY)

demand.title: How to move Car (.obj File) on Map [Solved]
Syncing a GLTF car model with Cannon-es
Optimizing material count on a car glb model

categories.notes:
Driving a car means turning its wheels, and here the conversion matters: when the library converted these files it flattened their node trees and merged every static part drawn with the same material, so in many cars the four wheels became one mesh, or part of the body. Load a pick with `model_run` and `model_look` lists every mesh with its name and size; on an open page, `eval` can call `scene.getObjectByName()`. GLTFLoader changes names as it loads them: spaces become underscores and dots are dropped. Where the wheels are joined, move the car as one rigid body and spin wheel models of your own, or pick another car.

For physics with cannon-es or Rapier, give the body a box collider sized from `new THREE.Box3().setFromObject(car)`, not the mesh, and copy the body's position and quaternion onto the model after each step. The median car stands 1.4 m tall, already scaled to life, and because same-material parts were already merged, each material it carries is about one draw call.

categories.title: Free truck 3D models for three.js (GLB, CC BY)
categories.notes:
Trucks often carry moving parts a game wants: a dump bed that tips, forklift forks that rise, a tow arm. Such a part keeps its own node when the source file animated it; otherwise the converter may have merged it into the chassis wherever the two shared a material. Check with `model_look` after loading the file through `model_run`, which names each mesh. A part's pivot is rarely where it should hinge: put a `THREE.Group` at the hinge, move the part into it with `attach()`, which keeps its world position, and rotate the group.

For a vehicle configurator, change paint by finding the body's material by name and setting its `color`, or give it a new texture with `colorSpace = THREE.SRGBColorSpace` and `flipY = false`, as glTF textures expect. Trucks run heavier than cars, a median of 11,700 triangles, and the median one is 2.5 m high, so measure a fleet's frame cost with `perf` before adding more.

categories.title: Free tank 3D models for three.js (GLB, CC BY)
categories.notes:
A tank game turns the turret about the vertical axis and raises the barrel about the turret's side axis, so the barrel must be a child of the turret. After the converter flattened these files, the turret and barrel sit beside the hull at the top of the scene, when they survived as separate meshes at all. Find them with `model_look` (after `model_run` loads the file), then rebuild the chain in code: a `THREE.Group` at the turret ring holding the turret, and a second group at the barrel's base holding the barrel, each filled with `attach()` so nothing jumps.

Tracks can roll by scrolling their texture when they have a material of their own: set the track map's `wrapS` to `THREE.RepeatWrapping` and add to `map.offset.x` as the tank moves. Tanks here are heavy for game props, a median of 16,400 triangles with nine in ten under 1.6 MB, so for an army run `model_audit` and fill the ranks with the low-poly ones (121 of them).

categories.title: Free boat 3D models for three.js (GLB, CC BY)

demand.title: Parametric Boat with Dynamic Water Masking
3D boat game where you recycle trash

categories.notes:
A boat's pivot is at its keel's bottom, so placed at the water's height it rides on the tip of its keel. Lower it by its draft, roughly a third of the hull's height for a small boat, which `new THREE.Box3().setFromObject(boat)` lets you measure.

To float on waves, sample your wave function at a few points under the hull (bow, stern and both sides) each frame, then set the boat's height from their average and its pitch and roll from their differences; easing toward those targets with a damped spring stops it snapping. Water showing inside an open hull is fixed with a mask: a mesh matching the hull's inner opening, with `colorWrite: false` and a lower `renderOrder` than the water, writes depth so the water behind it is not drawn. Sails and rigging on the larger ships are often alpha-cut cards that need `alphaTest` and `THREE.DoubleSide`. The median boat here is 5 m tall, mast included.

categories.title: Free airplane 3D models for three.js (GLB, CC BY)

demand.title: How can I make my airplane animaton smoother?

categories.notes:
Flight code needs to know which way the nose points, and authors disagree: some face +Z, some face along x. Check a loaded plane with `look`, then wrap the model in a `THREE.Group`, turned so the nose faces the group's forward axis, and steer the group, never the model inside. Turn with local rotations (`rotateX` for pitch, `rotateZ` for roll, `rotateY` for yaw) so the axes follow the plane. For a chase camera, move it toward a point behind the plane with `position.lerp()` and `quaternion.slerp()`, using a factor scaled by the frame's delta, which smooths the jitter a camera locked rigidly to the plane shows.

Of these, 70 are animated, usually a spinning propeller or landing gear. Animated parts kept their own nodes through the library's conversion, so an `AnimationMixer` plays them. On a static model the propeller has likely been merged into the nose; replace it visually with a blurred, alpha-tested disc that you rotate.

categories.title: Free drone 3D models for three.js (GLB, CC BY)

demand.title: Drone Simulator in Three.js: Real-Time Control and Animation

categories.notes:
Drones are small (the median is 0.5 m) and mostly sci-fi (116 of the 174), so an FPV camera needs a near plane short enough not to clip the frame: lower `camera.near` well below its default and add the camera as a child of the drone, a little ahead of its centre. A quadcopter's motion reads from its tilt: pitch it forward as it speeds up, roll it into turns, then ease back to level, and add a small hover bob with a sine of time so it never looks parked in the air.

Rotors are where these files differ. Of the 34 animated drones, those whose clip spins the rotors kept each rotor as its own node. In a static drone the conversion may have fused the rotors with the body; spin a translucent disc of your own over each mount instead. Status lights read better with `emissive` set on their material and a touch of bloom from `UnrealBloomPass`.

Emissive light reaches no other surface, so put a `PointLight` at the nozzle to light the hull around it. Where a ship has no separate engine material, add a small cone or sprite of your own behind each nozzle.

Space scenes run into float precision: far from the origin, vertices jitter as the camera moves. Keep the player's ship near the origin and move the universe around it. Ships here are modest in size, a median of 4 m tall, so a capital ship needs a `height` at pick time or a scale of your own. demand.title: Castle Builder - a multi-user WebXR sandbox experience
How implement a walk-through or exploration feature for model (such as a "castle" model)

categories.notes:
A castle is a building you walk around and often into, so collision matters more than for other props. The three.js addons hold the pieces: build an `Octree` from the castle with `octree.fromGraphNode(gltf.scene)` (from `three/addons/math/Octree.js`), move the player as a `Capsule` (`three/addons/math/Capsule.js`), and test it with `octree.capsuleIntersect()` each step, as the games_fps example does. Walls, stairs and ramps then work with no physics engine. `fromGraphNode` reads each mesh's geometry with its world matrix and ignores instance matrices, so collide against instanced walls through a merged copy or simple boxes.

Battlements, towers and posts that appeared five or more times in a source file were turned into GPU instances by the converter, and GLTFLoader loads those as an `InstancedMesh`, so a long wall stays cheap. The median castle here reaches 12 m. A stylized look dominates (132 of the 198 that pass), and many are toy-like or blocky, so choose by the style of the rest of your scene.

categories.title: Free windmill 3D models for three.js (GLB, CC BY)
categories.notes:
The point of a windmill is its turning sails. In the 16 animated files the sails kept their own node and the clip turns them: play it with an `AnimationMixer` and set `timeScale` on the action to match your wind. In a static windmill the sails may have been merged into the tower where they shared its material; where they did not, they are a separate mesh you can turn, but its origin is probably not at the hub. Measure the hub with `new THREE.Box3().setFromObject(sails).getCenter(new THREE.Vector3())`, put an empty `Object3D` there, move the sails into it with `attach()` and spin that pivot.

For a field of windmills, give the towers one `InstancedMesh` and the sails another, with the sail geometry centred on its hub, and turn every sail in the vertex shader by time: a hundred windmills then cost two draw calls and no matrix updates per frame. A median height of 10 m suits a landscape view, where they read from afar.

Scaling and positioning in Door Configurator

categories.notes:
A door swings on its hinge, but each file's origin sits at the bottom centre of its bounds, half a door's width from the hinge. Put an empty `THREE.Group` at the hinge edge (the minimum or maximum x of `Box3.setFromObject`), move the door into it with `attach()` so it keeps its place, and rotate the group about y to open it. Sci-fi doors (23 here) usually slide instead: move their panels sideways along the door's plane.

The 23 animated doors carry their own clip: play it with `action.setLoop(THREE.LoopOnce)` and `action.clampWhenFinished = true` so the door stays open, then run it with a negative `timeScale` to close it. For a door in a wall, leave a gap in the wall's geometry or cut one with the `three-bvh-csg` library; a door set into a solid wall has the wall drawn straight through it. At 2.1 m for the median door, size the wall opening to the door, not the reverse.

categories.notes:
Barrels are light: the median one has 1,160 triangles and nine in ten files are at most 0.5 MB, so the texture is most of what you download and most of what you see. A typical barrel is 0.9 m high, true to life, so it sits right in a level built at person scale.

As props they repeat, stacked in cellars and lined along docks: place them through an `InstancedMesh` per mesh, each copy spun to its own angle around y so the same stave pattern does not repeat in a row. For physics, a cylinder collider matches the shape, and a barrel knocked onto its side rolls on it as a box never would. These 351 models are all CC0: no credit is required, and you may change and sell them. `asset_search` still writes a line to `CREDITS.md` with each pick, which you can keep as a courtesy or delete.

Most come from museum collections: 204 are scans and 139 realistic models of vessels, tools, insects and statues, with no rigged models and 4 animated. They are dense, with a median of 62,900 triangles, so a gallery of several should be checked with `model_audit` and paced with `perf`.

A museum piece shows well on a turntable: `OrbitControls` with `autoRotate`, an environment map for soft light, and the camera framed to the model's bounds from `new THREE.Box3().setFromObject(model)`. The median object is 0.25 m tall, so set the camera's near plane small enough for a close look. `look` with `target` pictures one model from several sides.

categories.title: Free animated 3D models for three.js (GLB, CC BY and CC0)

demand.title: Can I apply a mixamo animation to another model that has already been rigged?
How to play animation not circular (animate with scroll)

categories.notes:
Animated does not always mean a character here: a trolley, storage boxes, a computer and a solar system move too, by node animation that an `AnimationMixer` plays as it plays a skeleton. Of the 4,921, 3,350 are rigged.

A one-shot animation, such as a lid opening on a click, plays with `setLoop(THREE.LoopOnce)` and `clampWhenFinished = true`, and `reset().play()` runs it again. For an animation driven by scroll instead of time, call `action.play()` and set `action.paused = true`, then on each scroll set `action.time = progress * clip.duration` and call `mixer.update(0)`.

A clip made for one skeleton plays on another when the bone names match. Every frame needs `mixer.update(dt)` with the time since the last frame, from `THREE.Timer` or `performance.now()`. The heights here vary widely, from small props to an entry listed at 60 m, so check each card's height before you place it.
